question: Should OpenClaw core own a per-agent backup/restore/clone workflow, and what credential/session portability contract should that workflow enforce?
rationale: The feature rewrites core config, per-agent SQLite state, credentials, workspaces, and transcripts, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security policy from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design core per-agent restore
options.body: Sponsor a core design that extends backup/restore with explicit `--agent` and `--as` semantics, credential/session policy, rollback, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Fold into broader backup work
options.body: Keep this issue open but require the broader backup/restore effort or encrypted snapshot PR to own per-agent scope before implementation.

options.title: Defer clone semantics
options.body: Limit near-term work to safer whole-install backup/restore docs and leave per-agent clone unsupported until multi-agent state policy matures.

recommendation.title: Design core per-agent restore
recommendation.body: Sponsor a core design that extends backup/restore with explicit `--agent` and `--as` semantics, credential/session policy, rollback, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup path-plan work plus repository policy on security-sensitive state makes this the strongest available routing candidate for a product/security decision.
